controls.detail: Run the same agent on multiple nominally identical robots.

controls.name: Cross-lab/site local baseline (LRR)
controls.detail: Each lab first reproduces the original setup to establish a local baseline before testing a new method.
controls.rules_out: Site-specific factors or incomparable absolute metrics across labs.
evidence: Integrated Benchmarking and Design for Reproducible and Accessible Evaluation of Robotic Agents

controls.name: Functionality-isolating tasks (FBMs)
controls.detail: Design tasks to engage only the subsystem under test and fix other factors (e.g., pre-positioning).
controls.rules_out: Attribution of success/failure to unrelated subsystems.
evidence: Competitions for Benchmarking: Task and Functionality Scoring Complete Performance Assessment

controls.name: External ground-truth sensing
controls.detail: Use motion capture or other external measurements during evaluation.
controls.rules_out: Apparent accuracy due to onboard sensing/odometry drift or bias.
evidence: Competitions for Benchmarking: Task and Functionality Scoring Complete Performance Assessment

controls.name: Standardized human stimuli
controls.detail: Hold human factors constant (e.g., same live speaker, fixed prompts).
controls.rules_out: Performance differences driven by human variability rather than system capability.
evidence: Competitions for Benchmarking: Task and Functionality Scoring Complete Performance Assessment

controls.name: Default-parameter simulator baselines across engines
controls.detail: Run default settings across multiple physics engines as reference conditions.
controls.rules_out: Effects stemming from protocol/dataset handling rather than simulator physics/modeling choices.
evidence: Benchmarking Simulated Robotic Manipulation Through a Real World Dataset

controls.name: Modality ablations
controls.detail: Evaluate with vision-only, language-only, and uninformed inputs alongside full V+L+A.
controls.rules_out: That performance derives solely from one modality or from priors without provided context.
evidence: DriveAction: A Benchmark for Exploring Human-like Driving Decisions in VLA Models
When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs

controls.name: Navigation-information ablation
controls.detail: Compare behavior with vs without navigation instructions in decision tasks.
controls.rules_out: Correct actions explained by image cues or priors rather than goal-aligned guidance.
evidence: DriveAction: A Benchmark for Exploring Human-like Driving Decisions in VLA Models

controls.name: Pretrained base vs fine-tuned model
controls.detail: Compare to the unfine-tuned backbone and to other models fine-tuned with their default recipes.
controls.rules_out: Improvements arising from the base model or generic fine-tuning rather than the proposed recipe.

Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

controls.name: Strong published baselines / prior SOTA on same benchmark
controls.detail: Compare against prior best numbers or strong baselines under identical protocols.
controls.rules_out: Gains due to evaluation protocol differences rather than actual performance.
evidence: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success
Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

controls.name: Component/penalty ablations for constrained RL
controls.detail: Compare mapping/projection layers with/without violation penalties and alternative mappings.
controls.rules_out: Effects explained purely by added penalties or specific solvers rather than the proposed mechanism.

confounds.name: Run-to-run randomness
confounds.detail: Stochasticity and transient variability can mimic improvements/failures.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Within-condition repeated trials/seeds with mean and dispersion reporting.
evidence: Competitions for Benchmarking: Task and Functionality Scoring Complete Performance Assessment
Integrated Benchmarking and Design for Reproducible and Accessible Evaluation of Robotic Agents

confounds.name: Hardware variation between robots
confounds.detail: Manufacturing/calibration differences alter outcomes independent of the method.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Cross-robot evaluations and detailed hardware reporting for replication.
evidence: Guest Editorial Open Discussion of Robot Grasping Benchmarks, Protocols, and Metrics
Integrated Benchmarking and Design for Reproducible and Accessible Evaluation of Robotic Agents

confounds.name: Sensor/viewpoint differences
confounds.detail: Different modalities/viewpoints/FOV/noise change perception results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report sensor models and viewpoint configuration; standardize/calibrate across runs.
evidence: Guest Editorial Open Discussion of Robot Grasping Benchmarks, Protocols, and Metrics

confounds.name: Lighting/environment effects
confounds.detail: Lighting level/type and environment conditions affect sensing and success.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report lighting (e.g., lux, structured vs ambient) and test under specified conditions.
evidence: Guest Editorial Open Discussion of Robot Grasping Benchmarks, Protocols, and Metrics

confounds.name: Lab/operator/infrastructure differences
confounds.detail: Site-specific nuances can shift results, making absolute numbers incomparable.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Cross-site reproduction with local baselines (LRR) and replicated experiments.
evidence: Integrated Benchmarking and Design for Reproducible and Accessible Evaluation of Robotic Agents
Towards Using Multiple Iterated, Reproduced, and Replicated Experiments with Robots (MIRRER) for Evaluation and Benchmarking

confounds.name: Object set selection and initial configuration sampling
confounds.detail: Choice of objects/poses can change task difficulty and measured performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use published sets (e.g., YCB) and specify exact configuration sampling procedures.
evidence: Competitions for Benchmarking: Task and Functionality Scoring Complete Performance Assessment
Guest Editorial Open Discussion of Robot Grasping Benchmarks, Protocols, and Metrics

confounds.name: Training–test leakage or overfitting
confounds.detail: Overlap or overfitting drives apparent gains without generalization.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Strict train/test separation; monitor held-out validation losses/metrics.
evidence: Guest Editorial Open Discussion of Robot Grasping Benchmarks, Protocols, and Metrics
Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

confounds.name: Data integrity and failed runs bias aggregates
confounds.detail: Including aborted/invalid runs or corrupted logs skews metrics.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Hardware compliance checks; data validation; include only successful validated runs.
evidence: Integrated Benchmarking and Design for Reproducible and Accessible Evaluation of Robotic Agents

confounds.name: Averaging masks multimodal outcomes
confounds.detail: Averaging trajectories hides distinct terminal pose modes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare distributions over repeated trials (e.g., Mahalanobis distance of final poses).
evidence: Benchmarking Simulated Robotic Manipulation Through a Real World Dataset

confounds.name: Controller/actuator mismatch vs physics differences
confounds.detail: Discrepancies attributed to physics may stem from controller dynamics or loop rates.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Match control modes, limits, and loop rates to the dataset; prescribe controller parameters.
evidence: Benchmarking Simulated Robotic Manipulation Through a Real World Dataset

confounds.name: Missing contacts / faulty contact dynamics
confounds.detail: Large errors arise from missed or unstable contacts rather than nominal parameters.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure contact forces/moments, wrist F/T, torques, and moving time to detect contact failures.
evidence: Benchmarking Simulated Robotic Manipulation Through a Real World Dataset

confounds.name: Timing ambiguity due to parallelism
confounds.detail: Parallel sensing/computation/motion alters effective cycle time and MPPH.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report t_s, t_c, t_r separately and note parallel vs sequential execution.
evidence: Guest Editorial Open Discussion of Robot Grasping Benchmarks, Protocols, and Metrics

confounds.name: Capabilities come from pretrained VLM features, not action learning
confounds.detail: Vision-language pretraining alone could explain performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Initialize from VLM-only weights and compare out-of-the-box task success to action-pretrained models.
evidence: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

confounds.name: Post-training dominates pre-training scale effects
confounds.detail: Alignment/post-training may overwrite pre-training benefits.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Post-train from checkpoints with varied pre-training scales and compare held-out/task success.
evidence: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

confounds.name: Visual shortcuts (attractors) cause failures, not language weakness
confounds.detail: Salient training-task objects bias policies regardless of instructions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Remove visual attractors (CF-Focused) and measure grounding/success changes.
evidence: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs

confounds.name: Generic language incapacity explains counterfactual failures
confounds.detail: Models may just not follow language at all.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Show strong in-domain instruction following and restored grounding when attractors are removed.
evidence: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs

confounds.name: Improvements from degraded/random behavior
confounds.detail: Method perturbs behavior, trading off competence for apparent grounding gains.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report both grounding and task success; demonstrate preserved/improved in-domain success.
evidence: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs

confounds.name: Simple training tricks replicate effects
confounds.detail: Vanilla language dropout could explain gains.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Ablations with dropout showing degradation vs proposed method.
evidence: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs

confounds.name: Idle/noisy trajectory segments bias learning
confounds.detail: Long idle periods teach trivial/no-op actions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Filter idle segments from training data and re-evaluate.
evidence: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

confounds.name: Human-judging subjectivity
confounds.detail: Subjective scoring inflates/deflates performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Automated RefBoxes and objective sensing/ground truth for scoring.
evidence: Competitions for Benchmarking: Task and Functionality Scoring Complete Performance Assessment

confounds.name: Hardware heterogeneity biases logged data
confounds.detail: Different sensors/actuators embed biases in shared datasets/logs.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Precisely specify arenas/objects/ground truth and release common logs for offline comparison.
evidence: Competitions for Benchmarking: Task and Functionality Scoring Complete Performance Assessment

confounds.name: Zero-gradient from closest-point projection
confounds.detail: Actor gradients vanish, making projection-based RL seem ineffective.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate alternative mappings (α-projection, radial, NFW) and compare learning outcomes.
evidence: Benchmarking Actor-Critic Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Robotics Control with Action Constraints

confounds.name: Computational overhead explains poor practicality
confounds.detail: Optimization layers cause slow training rather than poor learning quality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report CPU/GPU wall-clock runtimes alongside rewards for fair comparison.
evidence: Benchmarking Actor-Critic Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Robotics Control with Action Constraints

confounds.name: Batch size/solver availability differences
confounds.detail: Unavailable/altered batch sizes confound algorithm comparisons.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Run additional experiments at common feasible batch sizes and report separately.
evidence: Benchmarking Actor-Critic Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Robotics Control with Action Constraints

confounds.name: Projection solver failures for distant outputs
confounds.detail: QP solver fails on extreme actions, biasing results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Apply output squashing before projection and verify successful projections during rollouts.
evidence: Benchmarking Actor-Critic Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Robotics Control with Action Constraints

confounds.name: Missing navigation/context yields hallucinated actions
confounds.detail: Absent goal context leads to plausible but wrong decisions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Ablate navigation inputs and compare action accuracy in targeted scenarios.
evidence: DriveAction: A Benchmark for Exploring Human-like Driving Decisions in VLA Models

confounds.name: Dataset coverage imbalance
confounds.detail: Overrepresentation of easy maneuvers inflates overall accuracy.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Curate broad scenario coverage and analyze per-task performance to expose weaknesses.
evidence: DriveAction: A Benchmark for Exploring Human-like Driving Decisions in VLA Models

confounds.name: Cross-benchmark label ambiguity
confounds.detail: Score drops due to ambiguous/mislabeled items in other datasets.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Manual audits identifying and excluding erroneous/ambiguous cases in comparisons.
evidence: DriveAction: A Benchmark for Exploring Human-like Driving Decisions in VLA Models

confounds.name: A priori knowledge biases HRI questionnaires
confounds.detail: Participants’ prior familiarity drives ratings independent of interaction quality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Record prior knowledge and analyze group-wise effects in the statistical evaluation.
evidence: Tabulation and analysis of questionnaire results of subjective evaluation of seal robot at Science Museum in London

experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Select 3 standard RoboDojo tasks. For each task, run >=5 random seeds with >=10 episodes per seed (>=50 episodes/task). Compute per-task mean success rate and standard error across episodes. Pass if these statistics are computed and stored for all 3 tasks; otherwise fail.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Repeatability with statistics is a foundational norm; it is cheap to verify in simulation and immediately refutes claims of standard practice if absent.

experiment_recipes.goal: Train/test split and sampler compliance on LIBERO
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Explicit train/test separation and trial reporting
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Evaluate only on LIBERO (eval) tasks with the policy frozen (no gradient updates) and with object initial states sampled using the published LIBERO evaluation sampler. For each of 3 tasks, run >=50 episodes and write metadata containing sampler parameters, number of trials, and seed list. Pass if: (a) evaluation logs show zero training steps on LIBERO (eval), and (b) metadata contains the sampler spec and N_episodes >=50 for all tasks; otherwise fail.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Strict train/test separation and explicit reporting of trials and sampling are core experimental norms that can be verified by attempting compliant evaluation and inspecting logs/metadata.

experiment_recipes.goal: Validated external mocap for ground truth
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Set up external mocap (e.g., Qualisys/OptiTrack) and register it to robot frames. Using a calibration tool or end-effector probe, collect >=100 diverse stationary poses spanning the workspace and compare mocap poses to robot forward-kinematics ground truth. Pass if median translation error <= 5 mm and median rotation error <= 0.5 deg; otherwise fail.
constraints_not_enforced: Repeatability with statistics in manipulation tasks
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ground-truth apparatus must be validated before headline tests; numeric accuracy gates ensure the apparatus provides reliable pose references as required by norms.

metrics: sensing/computation/motion time per attempt (t_s, t_c, t_r) (lower_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Choose 3 RoboCasa tasks available in both simulation and a corresponding real-robot setup. Use the same object set and initial-state sampler in both domains. Run >=50 episodes per task in sim and >=30 episodes per task on the real robot. Log rosbag/sensor streams, videos, and (from the validated apparatus) mocap ground truth; match control-loop and logging rates to >=10 Hz and record t_s, t_c, t_r per attempt. Pass if, for all tasks, sim and real trials are completed with identical sampling specs, and mean±SE of success rate, moving time, and t_s/t_c/t_r are reported from the collected logs; otherwise fail.
depends_on: Validated external mocap for ground truth
experiment_recipes.rationale: Norms require sim-to-real testing on matched tasks with comprehensive logging and timing; this directly verifies those requirements using standardized benchmarks and validated ground truth.

experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Deploy the same frozen policy binary on two nominally identical robots of the same platform. On a fixed 5-task YCB manipulation suite, run >=20 episodes per task per robot using automated scoring (Competition-style multi-run scoring with automation). Record identical sensor configurations and calibrations, and capture rosbag/videos/mocap logs. Pass if per-robot mean±SE success rates for each task are computed and all raw logs are saved for both robots; otherwise fail.
depends_on: Validated external mocap for ground truth
experiment_recipes.rationale: Running the same agent on multiple identical robots and reporting variability is a key norm to rule out idiosyncratic hardware effects.

experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if the following all succeeded: (1) Repeatability in RoboDojo (statistics), (2) Train/test split and sampler compliance on LIBERO, and (3) Sim-to-real on matched RoboCasa tasks—yielding standardized success-rate summaries across at least these three distinct benchmarks; otherwise fail.
depends_on: Train/test split and sampler compliance on LIBERO
experiment_recipes.rationale: Evaluating across multiple established benchmarks is a generality norm; this control aggregates prior tasks to ensure cross-benchmark coverage under consistent reporting.
